newsitem.title: FRANCE: France, Britain to meet on EU, Zaire discord.
newsitem.headline: France, Britain to meet on EU, Zaire discord.

text.p: French and British leaders will seek to iron out discord over the European Union at a summit on Thursday at which Paris will also press London to offer troops for a proposed force to protect refugees in Zaire.

French President Jacques Chirac and British Prime Minister John Major start the two-day meeting over dinner at a restaurant in Bordeaux, the southwestern wine capital, amid tight security after a Corsican guerrilla attack in the city last month.

Major is expected to use the meeting to urge France and other European Union nations to strictly respect economic criteria laid down for EU economic and monetary union from 1999 or risk undermining the project.

Chirac, accompanied by Prime Minister Alain Juppe who is also Bordeaux's mayor, will say France respects the criteria set out in the EU's Maastricht treaty. Paris won European Commission backing this week for a 37.5 billion franc ($7.3 billion) pensions transfer by France Telecom to the state in a move that cuts the budget deficit.
"The question is no longer an issue. The president can say with his hand on the treaty that we are respecting it," Chirac spokeswoman Catherine Colonna said.
The two leaders, accompanied by about a dozen other ministers, will also debate Middle East peace efforts and policy over Bosnia.

Britain remains wary of French and Spanish proposals to send a multinational force of about 5,000 troops to help relief supplies reach more than a million refugees threatened by fighting in eastern Zaire.
British officials say they will listen to French proposals while stressing the vast problems of successful military action.
French Foreign Minister Herve de Charette lashed out at unnamed reluctant allies on Tuesday, saying in a television interview: "The main obstacle is the international community's spinelessness."

The idea of setting up a force gained ground on Tuesday with support from Zairean President Mobutu Sese Seko. Tutsi rebels who have overwhelmed the Zaire army in two eastern provinces say they would oppose French participation.

Chirac and Major, at their last bilateral summit before British elections due by May 1997, will also seek to smooth out differences on EU majority voting and French and German plans for flexibility to let some states integrate faster than others.
"Chirac says that Europe cannot truly be built without Britain," Colonna said.
The only concrete accord expected is a bilateral agreement to increase naval cooperation, which Colonna said was part of a drive towards a common European defence policy.

The two countries will sign a letter of intent to increase naval cooperation on issues ranging from arms procurement to training and computers. The pact, however, will not stretch to nuclear submarines or joint patrols.

The two countries last year set up a Franco-British air group near London to cover air force cooperation. Colonna said the move was a success and that Italy and Germany were now interested in taking part.
The British destroyer Liverpool will be docked in Bordeaux during the summit alongside the French frigate Latouche-Treville.
